terminal.description: A shell in the top folder. Run the setup once to build the stand-in for the shop's server, then clone it from here and work inside shop.

tasks.title: Clone the shop's repository into shop
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs` in the top folder. It builds `server/shop.git`, which stands in for the shop's server, and leaves `shop` empty: your laptop is new.

From the top folder, copy the server's repository into `shop` with Git, so that `shop` has the whole history and knows where the server is.

The check expects `shop` to be a repository with a remote called `origin` that points at `server/shop.git`, and a branch `main` with the server's history.
nextSteps: Run `node setup.mjs` and stay in the top folder.
Copy the server's repository with the command from the lesson, with `server/shop.git` as the address and `shop` as the folder.
Run `cd shop`, then `git remote -v`: `origin` points at the server.
Run `git status`: main is up to date with origin/main.
hints: A copy of a repository with its whole history and a link back to where it came from is called a clone.
`git clone` takes the address of the repository to copy, then the folder to put the copy in. Run it in the top folder, not inside shop.
In the top folder, run `git clone server/shop.git shop`.

tasks.title: Get Wilma's gift-vouchers branch onto your laptop
tasks.description:
Wilma started gift vouchers on a branch of the server, `gift-vouchers`. Your copy knows it as `origin/gift-vouchers`, but `git branch` lists only `main`.

Get a branch of your own called `gift-vouchers` that starts where the server's does and follows it.

The check expects a branch `gift-vouchers` in `shop` with Wilma's commit on it, following `origin/gift-vouchers`.
nextSteps: In `shop`, run `git branch -a`: `remotes/origin/gift-vouchers` is the server's branch.
Use the lesson's way to get a branch of your own from a branch of the server.
Read what Git prints: it says which branch yours is set up to track.
Run `git status`: up to date with `origin/gift-vouchers`.
hints: origin/gift-vouchers is Git's memory of the server's branch. You do not commit on it; you make a branch of your own from it.
Switching to a branch you do not have yet, when origin has one with that exact name, makes yours from it and has it follow the server's.

tasks.title: Commit the voucher fix on gift-vouchers, and keep it on your laptop
tasks.description:
On `gift-vouchers`, the voucher line in `shop/visit.html` says the vouchers never expire. They last two years. Change the last sentence of that line to:

```
They can be used for two years.
```

Save it and commit it on `gift-vouchers`. Change nothing else. Do not send it to the server: Wilma wants to read it first.

The check expects a commit on `gift-vouchers` after Wilma's whose voucher line says two years, no other change, and the server's `gift-vouchers` as it was.
nextSteps: Make sure `git status` says `On branch gift-vouchers`.
Change the sentence in `shop/visit.html` and save.
Stage and commit as always. If Git says `Author identity unknown`, this copy has no name and email yet: set them as in the first issue.
Run `git status`: your branch is ahead of `origin/gift-vouchers` by 1 commit.
hints: The voucher line is only on gift-vouchers. On main, visit.html does not have it.
A commit in your copy stays in your copy. Nothing reaches the server until you send it, so the usual edit, add and commit is all there is.
On gift-vouchers, change the sentence in the editor and save, then run `git add visit.html` and `git commit -m "Say that gift vouchers last two years"`.
